Where it began

Morné Morkel was born in Vereeniging on 6 October 1984, the youngest of three in a cricketing family. His older brother Albie also played for South Africa.

He was 19 when he made his first-class debut, for Easterns against the touring West Indians, and it was a lively start in every sense: he bowled 17 no-balls in one five-over spell. He did rather better with the bat, making an unbeaten 44 and adding 141 for the ninth wicket alongside Albie. His first wicket at that level was Ramnaresh Sarwan.

The player

His Test debut came in the Boxing Day Test at Durban in 2006, against India, when he took the place of Dale Steyn. Before long the two were bowling in tandem. With Steyn and Vernon Philander he made up a pace attack that Allan Donald, then South Africa's bowling coach, rated the finest the country had ever had.

In March 2018, against Australia, he became the fifth South African to reach 300 Test wickets. It was his final series. South Africa won the last Test by 492 runs and took their first home series against Australia since 1969–70. In all he played 86 Tests from 2006 to 2018 and took 309 wickets at 27.67, with a best of 6 for 23 and eight five-wicket innings.

What made him special

Height, pace and bounce were his gifts, and Donald, who knew something about fast bowling, praised his genuine speed. He was just as handy in the short game. At the first Twenty20 World Championship, in 2007, when plenty of people thought the format had little to offer bowlers, he took 9 wickets at 13.33, among them four for 17 against New Zealand. In the 2012 IPL he was the leading wicket-taker, with 25 for Delhi Daredevils.

He batted left-handed, and usefully, down the order. His 944 Test runs included a best of 40, so the unbeaten 44 from his first-class debut stayed just out of reach.

Away from the middle

He and Albie made a small piece of history in one-day cricket: when they shared the new ball, it was the first time two brothers had opened the bowling in an ODI. He played 117 ODIs and 44 T20 internationals.

After retiring he moved into coaching. He worked with Lucknow Super Giants, was Pakistan's bowling coach in 2023, and from August 2024 held the same job with India, who went on to win the 2025 Champions Trophy, the 2025 Asia Cup and the 2026 T20 World Cup. He married the Australian sports journalist Roz Kelly in December 2014.

And finally

Few fast bowlers can have made a noisier start in first-class cricket than 17 no-balls in five overs. His front foot learned its manners in time, and 309 Test wickets later nobody was counting the extras.
